title: Palindrome Cuts
statement:
Cut the string `text` into **pieces of consecutive letters** (the pieces together must give back the whole text, in order). A cutting is **good** if **every piece is a palindrome** (reads the same forwards and backwards). For example `aab` can be cut as `a|a|b` or `aa|b`, both good.

Return the **number of good cuttings**.
constraints: text contains only lowercase letters a-z

hints.nudge: Choose where the first piece ends. It must be a palindrome. What is left to cut afterwards?
hints.pattern: Backtracking over the end of the next piece; or dynamic programming over prefixes.
hints.walkthrough: Recursive version: from a start position, try every end position; if the piece is a palindrome, count the good cuttings of the rest. That recomputes the same suffixes, but with n <= 16 it is still fast. A faster idea: let ways[i] be the number of good cuttings of the first i letters. The last piece covers letters start..i-1; if it is a palindrome, it adds ways[start]. So ways[i] = sum of ways[start] over palindromic pieces ending at i. O(n^2) pieces, each checked in O(n).
